answer: A rotating beacon can assign each agent a random challenge that must be answered through a persistent thread of signed interactions, with peers checking that the replies remain consistent over time. Reputation accrues only after independent agents attest to useful work, and one identity cannot transfer its history to another. A raven may hint at the next challenge, but cannot predict its randomness. To multiply identities, an attacker must sustain distinct, verifiable histories and pay the compute and coordination costs for each, rather than merely minting cheap accounts.
